children.name: Varanus
children.description: Large to enormous predatory lizards with deeply forked tongues, powerful claws, and muscular bodies. Monitors actively hunt prey rather than ambushing it, using their long forked tongue to track scent trails. The Komodo Dragon is the largest lizard on Earth, capable of killing water buffalo.

children.name: Varanus komodoensis
children.description: The Komodo dragon (Varanus komodoensis), also known as the Komodo monitor, is a large reptile of the monitor lizard family Varanidae that is endemic to the Indonesian islands of Komodo, Rinca, Flores, Gili Dasami, and Gili Motang.

children.name: Varanus niloticus
children.description: The Nile monitor (Varanus niloticus) is a large member of the monitor family (Varanidae) found throughout most of Sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in drier regions, and along the Nile River and its tributaries in East Africa.

children.name: Varanus salvator
children.description:
The Asian water monitor (Varanus salvator) is a large varanid lizard native to South and Southeast Asia. It is widely considered to be the second-largest lizard species, after the Komodo dragon. It is distributed from eastern and northeastern India and Bangladesh, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Sri Lanka, through southern China and Hainan Island in the east to Mainland Southeast Asia and the islands of Sumatra, Borneo, Java, Lombok, the Riau Archipelago, and Sulawesi. It is one of the most widespread monitor lizards.
The Asian water monitor has a natural affinity towards water, inhabiting the surroundings of lakes, rivers, ponds, swamps, and various riparian habitats, including sewers, city parks, and urban waterways. It is an excellent swimmer and hunts fish, frogs, invertebrates, water birds, and other aquatic and amphibious prey.

children.name: Varanus varius
children.description: The lace monitor (Varanus varius), also known as the tree goanna, is a member of the monitor lizard family native to eastern Australia.

children.name: Varanus griseus
children.description: The desert monitor (Varanus griseus) is a species of monitor lizard of the order Squamata found living throughout North Africa and Central and South Asia.

children.name: Varanus exanthematicus
children.description: The savannah monitor (Varanus exanthematicus) is a medium-sized species of monitor lizard native to Africa.

children.name: Varanus acanthurus
children.description: The spiny-tailed monitor (Varanus acanthurus), also known as the Australian spiny-tailed monitor, the ridge-tailed monitor the Ackie dwarf monitor, and colloquially simply ackie monitor, is an Australian species of lizard belonging to the genus of monitor lizards (Varanus).

children.name: Varanus albigularis
children.description: The rock monitor (Varanus albigularis) is a species of monitor lizard in the family Varanidae.

children.name: Varanus bengalensis
children.description: The Bengal monitor (Varanus bengalensis), also called Indian monitor, is a species of monitor lizard distributed widely in the Indian subcontinent and parts of Southeast Asia and West Asia.

children.name: Varanus beccarii
children.description: The black tree monitor or Beccari's monitor (Varanus beccarii) is a species of lizard in the family Varanidae. The species is a relatively small member of the family, growing to about in total length (including tail). V. Beccarii is endemic to the Aru Islands off New Guinea, living in an arboreal habitat. The skin color of adults is completely black, to which one common name refers.

children.name: Varanus caerulivirens
children.description: The turquoise monitor (Varanus caerulivirens) is a species of monitor lizards found in Indonesia.

children.name: Varanus boehmei
children.description: The golden-spotted tree monitor (Varanus boehmei), also known commonly as the golden speckled tree monitor, is a species of monitor lizard in the family Varanidae. The species is endemic to Waigeo Island in Indonesia.

children.name: Varanus bogerti
children.description: Bogert's monitor (Varanus bogerti) is a species of tree-dwelling monitor lizard. The species is native to Papua New Guinea.

children.name: Varanus brevicauda
children.description: The short-tailed pygmy monitor (Varanus brevicauda) is the second smallest living monitor lizard in the world with a maximum length of 25 cm.

children.name: Varanus bushi
children.description: The Pilbara monitor (Varanus bushi), also known commonly as Bush's monitor, Bush's pygmy monitor, and the Pilbara mulga goanna, is a species of monitor lizard in the family Varanidae.

children.name: Varanus caudolineatus
children.description: The stripe-tailed goanna (Varanus caudolineatus), also known as the line-tailed pygmy monitor is a semi-arboreal species of monitor lizard native to Western Australia.

children.name: Varanus cumingi
children.description: The yellow-headed water monitor (Varanus cumingi), also commonly known as Cuming's water monitor, the Mindanao water monitor, and the Philippine water monitor, is a large species of monitor lizard in the family Varanidae. The species is endemic to the Philippines. It thrives in mangrove, forest and water margins in tropical refuges, where it feeds on birds, fishes, mammals, and carrion.

children.name: Varanus doreanus
children.description: The blue-tailed monitor, blue-tailed tree monitor or Kalabeck's monitor (Varanus doreanus), is a monitor lizard of the family Varanidae. It belongs to the V. Doreanus group of the subgenus Euprepiosaurus.

children.name: Varanus dumerilii
children.description: Dumeril's monitor (Varanus dumerilii), also known as the brown rough-necked monitor, is a species of lizard in the family Varanidae. The species is endemic to Southeast Asia.

children.name: Varanus eremius
children.description: The rusty desert monitor (Varanus eremius) is a species of small monitor lizards native to Australia. It is also known as the pygmy desert monitor. The monitor lizard belongs to the subgenus Odatria along with the pygmy mulga monitor. This monitor lizard is oviparous as with other monitor lizards.

children.name: Varanus finschi
children.description: Finsch's monitor (Varanus finschi) is a species of monitor lizard in the family Varanidae. The species is native to New Guinea and Australia.

children.name: Varanus flavescens
children.description: The yellow monitor (Varanus flavescens) or golden monitor is a monitor lizard native to South Asia.

children.name: Varanus giganteus
children.description:
The perentie (Varanus giganteus) is a species of monitor lizard. It is one of the largest living lizards, after the Komodo dragon, Asian water monitor, and the crocodile monitor. Found west of the Great Dividing Range in the arid areas of Australia, it is rarely seen because of its shyness and the remoteness of much of its range from human habitation. The species is considered to be a least-concern species according to the International Union for Conservation of Nature.
Its status in many Aboriginal cultures is evident in the totemic relationships, and part of the Ngiṉṯaka dreaming, as well as bush tucker. It was a favoured food item among desert Aboriginal tribes, and the fat was used for medicinal and ceremonial purposes.

children.name: Varanus gilleni
children.description: The pygmy mulga monitor (Varanus gilleni), also known commonly as Gillen's monitor or just the mulga monitor, is a species of lizard in the family Varanidae. The species is endemic to Australia.

children.name: Varanus glauerti
children.description: The Kimberley rock monitor (Varanus glauerti) is a medium-sized species of monitor lizard in the family Varanidae. The species is native to Northern Australia. Also known commonly as Glauert's monitor, Quinkan rock monitor and the Kakadu sand goanna, it belongs to the subgenus Odatria.

children.name: Varanus glebopalma
children.description: The black-palmed rock monitor (Varanus glebopalma) is a member of the Varanidae family found in Australia. Also known as the twilight monitor or the long-tailed rock monitor, it is a member of the subgenus Odatria, and is found in the northern part of Australia in the Northern Territory and Western Australia, as well as Queensland. Specifically, its distribution extends from Mount Isa in the east to the Kimberleys in the west. Its habitat is areas of rock escarpment, and large populations may be found in small areas.

children.name: Varanus gouldii
children.description: The sand goanna (Varanus gouldii), also known commonly as Gould's monitor, the racehorse goanna, and the sand monitor, is a species of large Australian monitor lizard in the family Varanidae.

children.name: Varanus hamersleyensis
children.description: The Southern Pilbara rock goanna (Varanus hamersleyensis), also known as the Hamersley Range rock monitor, is a dwarf member of the family Varanidae.

children.name: Varanus indicus
children.description: The mangrove monitor, mangrove goanna, or Western Pacific monitor lizard (Varanus indicus) is a member of the monitor lizard family with a large distribution from northern Australia and New Guinea to the Moluccas and Solomon Islands.

children.name: Varanus jobiensis
children.description: The peach-throated monitor (Varanus jobiensis), also known as the Sepik monitor, is a species of monitor lizard native to New Guinea.

children.name: Varanus juxtindicus
children.description: The Rennell Island monitor (Varanus juxtindicus) is a species of monitor lizards found in the Solomon Islands archipelago. It is also known as the Hakoi monitor. It belongs to the subgenus Euprepiosaurus along with the canopy goanna, the peach-throated monitor, Kalabeck's monitor, and others.

children.name: Varanus keithhornei
children.description: Varanus keithhornei, commonly known as the canopy goanna, Keith Horne's monitor, blue-nosed tree monitor, or Nesbit River monitor, is a species of monitor lizards native to northeast Australia.

children.name: Varanus kingorum
children.description: Kings' monitor (Varanus kingorum), also known commonly as Kings' goanna, Kings' rock monitor, and the pygmy rock monitor, is a small species of monitor lizard in the family Varanidae. The species is native to Australia.

children.name: Varanus kordensis
children.description: Varanus kordensis, the Biak tree monitor, is a member of the Varanidae family found on Biak Island in Indonesia.

children.name: Varanus mabitang
children.description: The Panay monitor (Varanus mabitang) is an endangered monitor lizard native to Panay Island in the Philippines.

children.name: Varanus macraei
children.description: Varanus macraei, also known commonly as the blue-spotted tree monitor and the blue tree monitor, is a species of monitor lizard endemic to the island of Batanta in Indonesia.

children.name: Varanus melinus
children.description: The quince monitor (Varanus melinus) is a species of monitor lizards endemic to Indonesia.

children.name: Varanus mertensi
children.description: Mertens' water monitor (Varanus mertensi) is a species of monitor lizard in the family Varanidae. The species is native to northern Australia, and is a wide-ranging, actively foraging, opportunistic predator of aquatic and riparian habitats. It is named after German herpetologist Robert Mertens.

children.name: Varanus mitchelli
children.description: Mitchell's water monitor (Varanus mitchelli) is a semiaquatic species of monitor lizard in the family Varanidae. The species is native to Australia, where it is found in the northern regions. It is on the IUCN Red List as a "Critically Endangered" species. It can be distinguished by the orange or yellow stripes along its neck and dark spots along its back. It is mainly carnivorous and eats small prey such as lizard, birds, and insects.

children.name: Varanus namoroka
children.description: A small, slender monitor restricted to the tsingy limestone karst of the Namoroka National Park in northwestern Madagascar; one of only two Varanus species in Madagascar. Threatened by very limited range and habitat degradation.

children.name: Varanus nebulosus
children.description: The clouded monitor (Varanus nebulosus) is a species of monitor lizard, native to Myanmar, Thailand and Laos, Vietnam, to West Malaysia, Singapore, Sumatra, and Java.

children.name: Varanus nuchalis
children.description:
The large-scaled water monitor (Varanus nuchalis) is a species of monitor lizard.
It is endemic to the Philippines, where it is found on the islands of Cebu, Ticao, Negros, Panay and Masbate.

children.name: Varanus obor
children.description: The sago monitor or torch monitor (Varanus obor) is a species of monitor lizards endemic to the Indonesian island of Sanana.

children.name: Varanus olivaceus
children.description: The Gray's monitor (Varanus olivaceus) is a large (180 cm, >9 kg) monitor lizard known only from lowland dipterocarp forest in southern Luzon, Catanduanes, and Polillo Island, all islands in the Philippines. It is also known as Gray's monitor lizard, butaan, and ornate monitor. It belongs to the subgenus Philippinosaurus. It is largely arboreal and extremely shy. The population of northern Luzon was formerly included in the Gray's monitor, but has been recognized as a separate species, the northern Sierra Madre forest monitor (V. Bitatawa), since 2010.

children.name: Varanus ornatus
children.description: The ornate monitor (Varanus niloticus ornatus) is a monitor lizard that is native to West and Middle Africa.

children.name: Varanus panoptes
children.description: The yellow-spotted monitor (Varanus panoptes), also known as the Argus monitor, is a monitor lizard found in northern and western regions of Australia and southern New Guinea.

children.name: Varanus pilbarensis
children.description: The Pilbara rock monitor (Varanus pilbarensis) is a small member of monitor lizard of the subgenus Odatria endemic to the Chichester Range in Western Australia.

children.name: Varanus prasinus
children.description: The emerald tree monitor (Varanus prasinus) or green tree monitor, is a small to medium-sized arboreal monitor lizard. It is known for its unusual coloration, which consists of shades from green to turquoise, topped with dark, transverse dorsal banding. This coloration helps camouflage it in its arboreal habitat. Its color also makes the emerald tree monitor highly prized in both the pet trade and zoos alike.

children.name: Varanus primordius
children.description: The northern blunt-spined monitor (Varanus primordius) is a species of lizard in the family Varanidae. The species is native to Australia's tropical Northern Territory. It is listed as Near Threatened on the IUCN Red List.

children.name: Varanus rainerguentheri
children.description: Varanus rainerguentheri, also commonly known as Günther's mangrove monitor and Rainer Günther's monitor, is a species of lizard in the family Varanidae.

children.name: Varanus rosenbergi
children.description: The Rosenberg's monitor (Varanus rosenbergi) is an Australian species of varanid reptile found in southern regions of the continent. They are large and fast predators with rugged bodies and long tails, having a combined length up to 1.5 metres, that will consume any smaller animal that is pursued and captured or found while foraging. They occur in the Australian Capital Territory, New South Wales, South Australia, Victoria, where it may be rare or locally common, and more frequently observed in Western Australia, where it is sometimes abundant.

children.name: Varanus rudicollis
children.description: The black rough-necked monitor (Varanus rudicollis) is a species of monitor lizard found in Southeast Asian countries of Thailand, Burma, and Malaysia.

children.name: Varanus salvadorii
children.description: The crocodile monitor (Varanus salvadorii), also known as the Papuan monitor or Salvadori's monitor, is a species of monitor lizard endemic to New Guinea.

children.name: Varanus scalaris
children.description:
Varanus scalaris is a small species of monitor lizard. It is often referred to as the banded tree monitor or the spotted tree monitor.
It is found in Western Australia and the Northern Territory. It was first described as a subspecies of the Timor monitor and was elevated to full species status by Glen Milton Storr in 1983. Later, the eastern subspecies of V. Scalaris similis was classified as its own species, leaving the banded tree monitor restricted to northwestern Australia.

children.name: Varanus semiremex
children.description: The rusty monitor (Varanus semiremex) is a small species of monitor lizard.

children.name: Varanus similis
children.description: Varanus similis, known commonly as the Similis monitor or spotted tree monitor, is a small species of monitor lizard found in Australia, Indonesia and Papua New Guinea.

children.name: Varanus sparnus
children.description: The Dampier Peninsula monitor or Dampier Peninsula goanna (Varanus sparnus), described in 2014, is the smallest known species of monitor lizard, growing up to with a length of almost and a SVL. It is believed to live only on the Dampier Peninsula of the Kimberley region in northern Western Australia. It is highly active, making it difficult to observe or photograph in the wild. It has short legs, an elongate body, a reddish-brown back with widely scattered black spots and "a ridged, circular and short prehensile tail."

children.name: Varanus spenceri
children.description: Spencer's goanna (Varanus spenceri), also known as the Spencer's monitor, is a species of Australian monitor lizard. It can be found in the Northern Territory and Queensland.

children.name: Varanus spinulosus
children.description: Varanus spinulosus, known commonly as the Solomon Island spiny monitor, Isabel monitor, is a species of monitor lizard.

children.name: Varanus storri
children.description: Storr's monitor (Varanus storri) is a species of monitor lizard in the family Varanidae.

children.name: Varanus telenesetes
children.description: Varanus telenesetes, the mysterious tree monitor, is an enigmatic monitor lizard that may actually represent a colour faded specimen of the green tree monitor.

children.name: Varanus timorensis
children.description: The Timor monitor (Varanus timorensis), also known as the spotted tree monitor, is a species of small monitor lizard which can be found in Timor, Rote, Savu and other nearby islands in Timor-Leste and Indonesia.

children.name: Varanus togianus
children.description:
The Togian water monitor (Varanus togianus) is a species of monitor lizard.
It is endemic to the Togian Islands of Sulawesi, Indonesia.

children.name: Varanus tristis
children.description: The black-headed monitor or black-tailed monitor (Varanus tristis) is a relatively small species of monitor lizards native to Australia. It is occasionally also called the mournful monitor, freckled monitor (Varanus tristis orientalis) or the racehorse monitor, a name it shares with the Gould's monitor due to their exceptional speed. It is placed in the subgenus Odatria.

children.name: Varanus yemenensis
children.description: The Yemen monitor (Varanus yemenensis) is a species of Varanus that lives in Yemen and southwestern Saudi Arabia.

children.name: Varanus flavirufus
children.description: A sandy or reddish-orange monitor widespread across the interior of Australia, formerly treated as a subspecies of V. gouldii. Favours red sand dunes and spinifex desert; an active forager that digs for buried prey including lizards and invertebrates.

children.name: Varanus caspius
children.description: A large, grey monitor of the arid lowlands and semi-desert east of the Caspian Sea, ranging through Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan into Afghanistan and Iran. Sometimes treated as a subspecies of V. griseus; one of Central Asia's largest reptiles.

children.name: Varanus douarrha
children.description: Varanus douarrha, the New Ireland monitor, is a species of lizard of the family Varanidae.

children.name: Varanus bitatawa
children.description: The Northern Sierra Madre forest monitor (Varanus bitatawa), also known by the local names bitatawa, baritatawa, and butikaw, is a large, arboreal, frugivorous lizard of the genus Varanus.
